text: In the book's Penrose diagram of the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime, the r = 0 singularity is timelike — it appears as vertical lines that an infalling observer can always maneuver to avoid.
explanation: False. The book stresses that the Schwarzschild singularity is spacelike, appearing as horizontal lines in the Penrose/Kruskal diagram and lying in the future of every interior observer; it is therefore unavoidable — 'in the future, not to the right'. A timelike, avoidable singularity is precisely the misconception the diagram corrects.
